summary: Host the AI worker at the app root and let the panel read a module-level status store, so the worker runs whether or not Settings is open

coordination.notes: Extends the existing owner aiWorkerHost.ts rather than adding a second host: the hook keeps its name, its refs and its three effects, and only the publication path changes from component state to a module-level store beside it. AiWorkerPanel stops calling the hook and reads that store, which is the whole defect - the worker only existed while the Settings sheet was mounted. App.tsx gains one line beside usePresentationBridgePublisher, the established precedent for a single-window root hook. Two judgment calls recorded here rather than asked: (1) the hook now returns void instead of AiWorkerStatus, because a root hook that returned live status would re-render the whole app once per tick - the store is the read path for everyone; (2) the hook reads character and bridgeConnected through useAppStore.getState() and useAppStore.subscribe rather than selector hooks, for the same reason - a selector subscription at the root re-renders the entire tree on every status frame, roughly once a second. That also removes the per-tick effect restart that trap 6 describes, and the default absent provider is now a module singleton rather than a fresh object per render, which was restarting the tick effect on every render.
